observations: Photo 0 shows two mono-crystalline solar panels leaning against an exterior wall, outdoors on a paved area.
Panels appear to be standard aluminium-framed modules; no visible wattage, brand, or model sticker is legible in the image.
A faint watermark reading 'IZUTECH SOLAR ENERGY' is overlaid on the photo, apparently the seller's own branding, not a manufacturer label on the panel.
No close-up of the junction box, back sheet, or rating label is provided.
No scale reference or size markers to estimate cell count or physical dimensions precisely.

claims.claim: Izutech solar energy specialize in all solar equipment such as inverter, panels, charge controller...
claims.evidence: General business description, not tied to a visible attribute of this specific item.

risks.risk: Wattage/power rating unknown, which is the primary price driver for solar panels.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the rating label/nameplate on the back of each panel showing wattage, voltage, and cell count.
risks.if_unproven: Cannot even set a worst-case price without this, since comparables range from ~42,000 to 155,000 NGN depending on wattage.

risks.risk: New vs used condition not stated or shown; micro-cracks, hotspots, or discoloration could reduce value.
risks.proof: Clear daylight photo of the full panel face and back, plus any visible scratches or cell damage.
risks.if_unproven: Price as used/worst condition once wattage is known.

risks.risk: Functionality (actual power output) unverified; panel could be degraded or dead.
risks.proof: Video or photo of a multimeter reading open-circuit voltage under sunlight.

risks.risk: Quantity and matching specs of the two panels not confirmed (could be mismatched models).
risks.proof: Photo showing both nameplates side by side.
risks.if_unproven: Price each panel individually at worst case, assume lowest matching spec.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the rating/nameplate label on each panel (wattage, voltage, cell count).
Photo or video of a voltage/current test under sunlight to confirm the panels work.
Clear full-frontal and back shots of both panels to check for cracks or damage.
Confirmation of brand/model if any markings exist on the frame or junction box.
response.reason: The photo shows two unlabeled solar panels with no readable wattage, brand, or model, and wattage is the key attribute that sets price among comparables ranging widely; a nameplate or spec photo is needed before even a worst-case price can be assigned.
